glossary.mode.k1: Drives the compute units to the limit with FMA instructions, like FIRESTARTER: the load that makes the CPU draw the most power and run the hottest. It tests cooling, power delivery (VRM) and how well the boost holds. Every block of calculations is compared with a reference.
glossary.mode.k1.name: Maximum load (FMA)
glossary.mode.k2: Fourier transforms (FFT) on data that fits in the core's cache. They stress the compute units and the L1/L2 caches: the classic test for finding an unstable core. The result must match the reference bit for bit.
glossary.mode.k2.name: Small FFTs · cores and cache
glossary.mode.k3: The same FFTs on data much larger than the cache, so in RAM. They stress the memory controller, the RAM and the CPU's internal links (for example Infinity Fabric). They use the RAM share set in the settings.
glossary.mode.k3.name: Large FFTs · memory
glossary.mode.k4: Alternates FFTs of different sizes, from the cache to RAM, like Prime95's «Blend»: it tests the hand-over between cache and memory.
glossary.mode.k4.name: Mixed (blend)
glossary.mode.k5: Exact 64-bit integer calculations with the NTT, the transform used to multiply huge numbers (as in y-cruncher). It stresses the integer multiplier and allows no tolerance: a single wrong bit is an error.
glossary.mode.k5.name: Exact integers (NTT)
glossary.mode.k7: Multiplications of large matrices, the Linpack calculation: the most sustained floating-point load, and a hot one. The result is checked exactly with Freivalds' method.
glossary.mode.k7.name: Linpack
glossary.mode.k8: Encryption (AES, SHA-256), checksums (CRC32C), compression and sorting: they test the CPU's specialised units and branch prediction, which the other tests barely use. The results are compared with known values.
glossary.mode.k8.name: Encryption and compression
glossary.mode.k9: Two cores at a time pass blocks of data with a checksum to each other: it tests cache coherence and the links between cores and between CCDs.
glossary.mode.k9.name: Core-to-core exchange
glossary.mode.k10: Writes bit patterns to RAM and reads them back: inversions, modulo 20, random data, address in address, copy with CRC. It works on the memory Windows grants the program, in 4 KB pages: it does not replace MemTest86, TestMem5 or Karhu.
glossary.mode.k10.name: Memory patterns (RAM)
glossary.mode.steady: All threads work at 100% without pauses: it tests heat and power draw.
glossary.mode.steady.name: Steady load
glossary.mode.variable: Work and short pauses chosen at random (10 to 500 ms), jumping from one test to another. It tests fast changes of voltage and frequency, where an undervolt or a Curve Optimizer setting often gives way.
glossary.mode.variable.name: Variable load
glossary.mode.ramp: The load climbs from 20 to 100% in 5% steps. If an error appears, the test reports the load level and the clock it happened at: many instabilities show up at partial load.
glossary.mode.ramp.name: Adaptive ramp
glossary.mode.alternate: The load keeps jumping between 100% and about 15%, in periods of 10 to 500 ms. It tests the GPU's power delivery and fast clock changes.
glossary.mode.alternate.name: Alternating load
glossary.mode.pauseResume: Every minute the load stops for 12 seconds and then restarts at full. It tests the jump from the low clock to the high one, where an overclock often gives way.
glossary.mode.pauseResume.name: Pause and resume
glossary.mode.light: One thread with pauses, which lets the boost climb to its highest. Many Curve Optimizer instabilities show up precisely at low load.
glossary.mode.light.name: Light load
glossary.mode.coreCycle: The test runs on a single physical core for a few minutes, then moves on to the next. This shows which core makes mistakes.
glossary.mode.coreCycle.name: One core at a time
glossary.mode.allCore: One thread for every logical processor: the highest load for heat and power draw.
glossary.mode.allCore.name: All cores
glossary.mode.pattern.moving_inversions: Writes a value, reads it back and replaces it with its opposite, forwards and backwards through all the memory.
glossary.mode.pattern.modulo20: Writes one value every 20 positions and something else elsewhere: a test the caches cannot hide.
glossary.mode.pattern.modulo20.name: Modulo 20
glossary.mode.pattern.random: Fills the memory with pseudo-random data from a seed and reads it back.
glossary.mode.pattern.random.name: Random data
glossary.mode.pattern.address: Every position holds its own address: it finds swapped rows and columns.
glossary.mode.pattern.address.name: Address in address
glossary.mode.pattern.crc_copy: Copies blocks from one area to another, computing the CRC during the copy, like stressapptest: it tests the memory while the data moves.
glossary.mode.pattern.crc_copy.name: Copy with CRC
glossary.isa.avx512: 512-bit vector instructions (Zen 4 and Zen 5, some Intel CPUs). It is a load of its own: an overclock stable with AVX2 may not be with AVX-512.
glossary.isa.avx512.name: AVX-512
glossary.isa.avx2: 256-bit vector instructions with FMA, in almost every CPU since 2013. It is the set programs use most.
glossary.isa.avx2.name: AVX2
glossary.isa.sse2: 128-bit vector instructions, in every 64-bit CPU. They run cooler and let the boost climb higher.
glossary.isa.sse2.name: SSE2
glossary.fft: Fast Fourier transform: a calculation that breaks data down into frequencies. It moves a lot of data and makes full use of the floating-point units.
glossary.fft.name: FFT
glossary.ntt: The exact, integer version of the FFT: it is used to multiply huge numbers.
glossary.ntt.name: NTT
glossary.linpack: The classic supercomputer test: it solves large systems of equations with matrix multiplications.
glossary.linpack.name: Linpack
glossary.fma: An instruction that does a multiplication and an addition at once: the calculation that draws the most power.
glossary.fma.name: FMA
glossary.smt: Every physical core runs two threads. «One core at a time» usually uses only one, because a core on its own reaches the highest boost.
glossary.smt.name: SMT / Hyper-Threading
glossary.ccd: A block of cores of an AMD CPU with its own L3 cache. CPUs with several CCDs have separate overclock settings for each.
glossary.ccd.name: CCD
glossary.coreType: In hybrid Intel CPUs the P-cores (performance) are fast and the E-cores (efficiency) use little power. The test tries the P-cores first.
glossary.coreType.name: P-cores and E-cores
glossary.coreNumber: «Core 0» is the first physical core, as in the BIOS Curve Optimizer. Ryzen Master counts from 1 (C01 = core 0). With cores disabled at the factory the BIOS numbering may skip a number.
glossary.coreNumber.name: Core number
glossary.apicId: The number the hardware uses to identify a logical processor. A WHEA error says which processor reported it, not necessarily which one caused it.
glossary.apicId.name: APIC ID
glossary.tjmax: The highest temperature the CPU allows. The thermal stop acts 5 °C below it, when Tjmax is known.
glossary.tjmax.name: Tjmax
glossary.thermalStop: The test stops by itself if the temperature goes over the threshold for two readings in a row.
glossary.thermalStop.name: Thermal stop
glossary.throttling: The CPU lowers its own frequency because it is too hot or drawing too much power.
glossary.throttling.name: Throttling
glossary.whea: The hardware errors Windows records. The «corrected» ones were already fixed by the hardware, but they say the system is at its limit.
glossary.whea.name: WHEA
glossary.curveOptimizer: The AMD setting that lowers the voltage of each core. A value set too low causes calculation errors, often at low load.
glossary.curveOptimizer.name: Curve Optimizer
glossary.pbo: Precision Boost Overdrive: AMD's automatic overclock, which raises the power limits and the boost.
glossary.pbo.name: PBO
glossary.expoXmp: RAM profiles that raise its frequency and timings. They are an overclock of the memory and of the controller.
glossary.expoXmp.name: EXPO / XMP
glossary.vrm: The motherboard circuit that powers the CPU. Under full load it heats up too.
glossary.vrm.name: VRM
glossary.cState: The idle states of the cores. Entering and leaving them changes the voltage abruptly.
glossary.cState.name: C-state
glossary.boost: The extra frequency the CPU reaches when it has headroom in heat and power.
glossary.boost.name: Boost
glossary.imc: The part of the CPU that talks to the RAM. With EXPO/XMP it runs faster than normal.
glossary.imc.name: Memory controller
glossary.cache: Small, very fast memories inside the CPU. L1 and L2 belong to each core, L3 is shared.
glossary.cache.name: L1, L2, L3 cache
glossary.check: Every time a calculation ends, its result is compared with the right one. The number says how many comparisons were made.
glossary.check.name: Check
glossary.reference: The right result, computed at the start on three different cores that must agree.
glossary.reference.name: Reference
glossary.seed: The number the test's data is generated from. With the same seed the test repeats identically.
glossary.seed.name: Seed
glossary.iteration: One full round of a phase's calculation.
glossary.iteration.name: Iteration
glossary.ramShare: The part of the free memory the RAM tests use. At least 2 GB are always left for Windows.
glossary.ramShare.name: RAM share
performance.objective.normal.hint: I want to know whether the PC handles long loads without overheating or miscalculating.
performance.objective.overclock.hint: I changed frequencies, voltages or Curve Optimizer and want to find the errors.
performance.risk.title: Before you start
performance.risk.body: A stress test pushes the CPU to the maximum: heat, power draw and fan noise go up. An overclock test can freeze or restart the PC: save your open work before you start it.
performance.warn.noService: Service not running: without the CPU temperature the thermal stop does not work.
performance.warn.wheaUnreadable: Hardware errors unreadable: the system log cannot be accessed.
performance.advice.core: With Curve Optimizer, you usually reduce that core's offset.
performance.run.title: Test in progress
performance.result.title: Result
glossary.vm: Windows runs inside a computer simulated by another program (for example Hyper-V, VMware or VirtualBox). Temperatures, power and hardware errors are often hidden, and the load goes through the simulated computer: the results say less than on a real PC.
glossary.vm.name: Virtual machine
performance.wizard.ram.low: Not available: there is too little free memory, the share is under 256 MiB.
performance.wizard.vm: temperatures, power and hardware errors may not be readable.
performance.wizard.running: A test is running: «Start» comes back when it ends.
performance.wizard.notConnected: The test status is not available yet: try again in a few seconds.
performance.warn.gpuShared: The integrated GPU uses the system RAM: the VRAM check will use at most 4 GB of it.
glossary.threads: The logical processors Windows sees: each one can run a piece of work. With SMT (Hyper-Threading) a physical core has two, so an 8-core CPU shows 16 threads.
glossary.threads.name: Threads
performance.wizard.error.no_cores: there is no usable core for the test.
performance.wizard.error.no_phases: the plan has no phases: include at least one mode.
performance.wizard.error.too_long: the plan is longer than 24 hours: reduce the minutes.
performance.wizard.error.unknown_core: the chosen core does not exist on this CPU.
performance.wizard.error.ram_budget: the RAM share is under 256 MiB: close some programs or raise the share in the settings.
glossary.phase: A part of the test: one kind of computation with one load mode, for a set time. The phases run one after another.
glossary.phase.name: Phase
performance.core.label: Core {core}
performance.warn.ramReduced: RAM share reduced: there was not enough free memory for all of it.
performance.warn.ramInsufficient: Not enough free memory: a RAM phase was skipped.
performance.event.reference_invalid: Phase {phase}: invalid reference, a defect of the program and not of the CPU
performance.event.k9_needs_two_cores: Phase {phase} skipped: the core-to-core exchange needs at least two cores
performance.event.ram_reduced: Phase {phase}: memory per thread reduced to {value}
performance.event.ram_insufficient: Phase {phase} skipped: not enough free memory
performance.event.whea_unreadable: WHEA errors unreadable: the system log cannot be accessed
performance.event.suspended: The PC went to sleep: test interrupted
performance.event.kernelPower41: The PC turned off without shutting down Windows (Kernel-Power 41)
performance.result.missing: Session not found: it may have been deleted.
performance.result.kind.mismatch: The result differed from the reference.
performance.result.kind.reference_disagr: The cores that compute the reference did not agree.
performance.result.kind.reference_invali: Invalid reference: a defect of the program, not of the CPU.
glossary.bugcheck: The record Windows leaves when it stops with a blue screen and restarts: the whole system crashed, not just the test.
glossary.bugcheck.name: BugCheck
glossary.kernelPower41: The event Windows records when it starts again without having been shut down properly, for example after a freeze, a sudden restart or a power cut.
glossary.kernelPower41.name: Kernel-Power 41
glossary.packagePower: How much power the whole CPU draws right now, in watts: the «package» includes the cores, the cache and the controllers.
glossary.packagePower.name: Package power
glossary.clock: The frequency the cores run at, in GHz: how many computing steps they take each second. It rises with boost and drops when the CPU gets too hot.
glossary.clock.name: Clock
performance.history.missing: This test is no longer saved.
performance.score.duration: About 2 minutes. Close heavy applications before you start.
performance.score.invalid: Calculation error during the benchmark: try the stress test.
performance.score.flag.battery: Measured on battery: the score may be lower.
performance.score.flag.thermal_throttle: The CPU reached its maximum temperature: the score may be lower.
performance.score.flag.busy_system: Other programs used more than 10% of the CPU during the measurement.
performance.score.flag.no_sensors: Service not running: the temperature was not checked during the measurement.
performance.score.provisional: Scale not calibrated yet: the points will change.
performance.score.error.busy: A stress test or a benchmark is already running.
performance.score.error.failed: The benchmark stopped before the end: no measurement was saved.
performance.score.error.start: The benchmark did not start: {reason}. Try reinstalling the app.
glossary.benchPoints: Points on a fixed scale, the same for every CPU: twice the points means twice the work done in the same time.
glossary.benchPoints.name: points
glossary.singleCore: One workload on one core, the fastest: it tells how quick a single core is, as in games and in programs that use few threads.
glossary.singleCore.name: single core
glossary.multiCore: A copy of the workload on every thread of the CPU, all at once: it tells how much work the whole CPU does.
glossary.multiCore.name: multi core
glossary.scaling: How much of the theoretical work really comes through when all the threads run: 100% would mean every thread is as fast as on its own. SMT, heat and shared memory bring it down.
glossary.scaling.name: multi-core scaling
glossary.referenceMark: The mark on the dial: it shows where the measurement chosen in the menu reaches, to compare it with the current one.
glossary.referenceMark.name: reference ▲
glossary.warmup: A first round that does not count: it brings the CPU up to speed and fills the caches.
glossary.warmup.name: warm-up
glossary.median: Of the three repetitions the middle one is kept: a single disturbance does not change the result.
glossary.median.name: median
glossary.bench.ntt: A transform with exact 64-bit integer arithmetic: it measures the integer multiplier.
glossary.bench.ntt.name: NTT (integers)
glossary.bench.hash: Computes the SHA-256 and CRC32C fingerprints of a block of data: it measures the dedicated cryptography and checksum instructions.
glossary.bench.hash.name: Hash
glossary.bench.compress: Compresses and decompresses text: it measures how branches and nearby memory are handled, as when opening an archive.
glossary.bench.compress.name: Compression
glossary.bench.sort: Puts a million bytes of numbers in order: it measures branches that are hard to predict.
glossary.bench.sort.name: Sorting
glossary.bench.fft: A Fourier transform in double precision: it measures the floating-point units, as in audio and simulation.
